subject.title: fix(doctor): preserve unparseable config instead of silently discarding it

question: Should unrecoverable unparseable configurations make every repair-mode doctor caller fail non-zero, including automated post-update doctor runs?
rationale: The data-preserving behavior is safer, but it deliberately removes an existing success/fallback outcome and may require operator action in automated update or repair workflows.

options.title: Accept fail-closed recovery
options.body: Merge the preservation behavior after confirming automated doctor callers surface the failure without obscuring the preserved-path recovery instructions.

options.title: Narrow the failure scope
options.body: Keep interactive `doctor --fix` fail-closed while defining a separate explicit outcome for automated post-update callers if those workflows cannot safely propagate the error.

recommendation.title: Accept fail-closed recovery
recommendation.body: Merge the preservation behavior after confirming automated doctor callers surface the failure without obscuring the preserved-path recovery instructions.

likelyOwner.reason: The same person has prior history in config fail-closed and prefixed-config recovery behavior and authored this proposed policy change.
